Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase. The Indians are in a huddle with KL Rahul doing all the talking. With no Ryan Rickelton in the side for this game, Aiden Markram walks out to open alongside Quinton de Kock. Arshdeep Singh will start the attack for India. Arshdeep to Markram with a slip in place. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the game is interestingly poised at the halfway mark. With dew likely to play a role later in the evening, India will want to strike early while there is still something on offer with the new ball under the lights. As for South Africa, they showed in Ranchi just how deep their batting goes. They will be mindful of keeping wickets in hand and setting up the chase. Back in a bit for the second essay.

Ruturaj Gaikwad is in for a chat. Shares that he was gutted to not perform in the previous match but today he is fortunate enough to perform well for the team. Adds that the condition of the track suited his style. Continues that it's a dream to bat with a player like Virat Kohli. He was guiding him throughout the inning about where to assess the gaps and when to go harsh on the bowlers. Ends up saying that before the game, they were planning to put over 350 on the board if they bat first, and they are very happy to get it. He also states that there was a lot of dew the previous night, and hopes that it's less today.

In the death overs, the South African pacers continued their strong fightback. They bowled into the pitch, took the pace off, and made scoring difficult for India. A crucial moment that might well come back to haunt the tourists was the dropped chance of KL Rahul on 46 by Matthew Breetzke. With Rahul and Jadeja being the last recognised pair, and Jadeja struggling to find any rhythm, a wicket at that stage could have made a significant difference to the eventual total.

During the middle overs, South Africa never managed to build sustained pressure. The Indian pair kept the scoreboard moving with regular ones and twos, punctuated by the occasional boundary. Gaikwad shifted gears after reaching his fifty, racing from 50 to 100 in just 25 balls to bring up his maiden ODI ton. Soon after, Kohli brought up his second consecutive century. South Africa finally enjoyed a productive phase when they dismissed both centurions, along with Sundar, in the space of a few overs. Nandre Burger limping off added to their concerns, but Aiden Markram stepped up admirably.

Earlier, after losing their 20th toss in a row in ODIs, India were asked to bat first. Unlike the track in Ranchi, it was not easy to hit through the line early on and felt two-paced, though it gradually improved as the innings progressed. Both Lungi Ngidi and Nandre Burger found some early swing, but their lack of control meant they gave away extras. By the end of the first Powerplay, the Proteas had sent both Indian openers back, but that was as good as it got for them through the majority of the middle overs. Virat Kohli picked up exactly where he had left off in Ranchi, while Ruturaj Gaikwad, after battling against the short ball early on, grew steadily in confidence.

India do end up with 358, but for the second game in a row, they will feel they left a few runs out there. With dew expected later in the evening, they would certainly have preferred a cushion of 15 to 20 extra runs, and now it will be up to their bowlers to ensure that the shortfall does not prove costly. 18 runs came off the final over, making it the most expensive over of the innings. In a way, that somewhat spoiled the good work South Africa had produced at the death up until that point. However, considering the Proteas were not at their best with either the ball or in the field for much of the innings, they will still feel they have restricted the hosts to a manageable total.

Ravindra Jadeja is very quick and he will come back for two and India do end on a high. Banged in short over off, KL Rahul hangs back and pulls it flat down to long on for a couple of runs. 18 runs off the final over, the most expensive one of the innings and India end with a big total of 358/5 on the board.

South Africa lacked discipline upfront but still managed to pick up a couple of wickets by the end of the first Powerplay. Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin! The umpires make their way out to the middle and the Proteas can be seen waiting eagerly near the boundary ropes before taking to the field. It will be the duo Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal to open the innings for India once again. Jaiswal will take strike, and it will be Nandre Burger to start proceedings with the ball. A couple of slips to begin with. Let's play...

South Africa (Playing XI) - Aiden Markram, Quinton de Kock (WK), Temba Bavuma (C) (In for Ryan Rickelton), Matthew Breetzke, Tony de Zorzi, Dewald Brevis, Marco Jansen, Corbin Bosch, Keshav Maharaj (In for Prenelan Subrayen), Nandre Burger, Lungi Ngidi (In for Ottneil Baartman).

India (Unchanged Playing XI) - Yashasvi Jaiswal, Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Washington Sundar, KL Rahul (C/WK), Ravindra Jadeja, Harshit Rana, Arshdeep Singh, Kuldeep Yadav, Prasidh Krishna.

India's captain, KL Rahul says the most pressure he feels is during the toss, and it has been a long time since they have won one. He jokes that he has been practising for it, but it clearly has not been working. Reflecting on the last game, he feels the team did really well and there were a lot of positives to take forward. He adds that it is about coming out and playing hard cricket. Mentions that South Africa pushed them in the previous match, so they know exactly what to expect. Shares that this is the time of the year when dew is almost guaranteed, and they have spoken about it in team meetings. Further says that picking up early wickets becomes even more important in such conditions. Looking at the surface, he feels the wicket looks good. Tells that the only reason teams prefer chasing here is mostly because of the impact of dew later in the evening. Informs that they are unchanged for this game.

The captain of South Africa, Temba Bavuma, says that they will bowl first. Adds that the surface looks a bit on the drier side and they are hoping that the dew settles in during the chase and batting becomes a bit easier. Reckons that the belief is still there and they would like to start well with the bat. Informs that there are three changes with Keshav Maharaj, Lungi Ngidi and himself coming in, but there's no change in the combination.
TOSS - Temba Bavuma is back for the Proteas. He calls it correctly, and South Africa have elected to BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Deep Dasgupta and Shaun Pollock are pitchside. Deep says that the boundaries are 67 meters on either side and 74 meters in front. Adds that the surface looks good on the side that he's standing on, but Shaun Pollock at the other end says that on his side, the surface looks patchy and there will be uneven bounce as well. Reckons that the match won't be as high-scoring as the first ODI and there might be some reverse swing on offer late in the innings. Deep ends by saying that there will be dew and affirms that the toss will be crucial.

South Africa, meanwhile, find themselves with something to prove. Their top order faltered under pressure in the previous match, but the fight shown by the middle order was a major positive. Matthew Breetzke, Marco Jansen and Corbin Bosch stepped up and nearly dragged the Proteas to an unlikely win. Temba Bavuma and Keshav Maharaj were rested for the first ODI, but both are expected to return in Raipur, which will come as a much-needed boost for the visitors. With the series on the line, this is the moment for South Africa to rediscover their bite. Buckle up, folks, this showdown has all the elements for another blockbuster. Stay tuned for the toss and further updates.

For India, the confidence in the camp will be sky-high. Virat Kohli’s masterclass in the previous match has not only lifted the dressing-room energy but also reaffirmed his reputation as an ODI giant. Alongside him, Rohit Sharma's fluent start and the steady middle-order rhythm, provided by skipper KL Rahul and Ravindra Jadeja, have given India the batting solidity they need. The way Arshdeep Singh and Harshit Rana bowled with the new ball in the first encounter would have pleased the Indian think tank. Kuldeep Yadav’s trickery kept South Africa on the back foot last time around, and he will once again be key to India maintaining their hold over the series.

Hello, and a very warm welcome to all the cricket fans joining us for the build-up. The stage is perfectly set at the Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Stadium in Raipur as India and South Africa gear up for the second ODI of this three-match series. India enter this match with momentum behind them, especially after their win in a thriller in Ranchi, while South Africa will be in search of a series-levelling win.

All eyes shift to the Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Cricket Stadium in New Raipur as India and South Africa lock horns in the second ODI, with the hosts holding a narrow 1-0 advantage. The series opener had all the ingredients of a classic - big scores, late twists and a nerve-wracking finish, setting the stage perfectly for another blockbuster encounter. India will be keen to press home their advantage early, while South Africa know that defeat here means that the series is over. For India, their biggest stars stood tall in Ranchi. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli were back to their dominant best, combining assurance with authority at the top. Rohit breezed to another fluent half-century and also etched his name into the record books by becoming the highest six-hitter in ODI history, going past Shahid Afridi. But it was the ‘Ko’ in RoKo who truly stole the spotlight - Kohli’s sublime 135 was a reminder of his enduring class, with the 52nd century of his ODI career looking as effortless as ever. That said, India would want more from Yashasvi Jaiswal, who has had a quiet start to the series, and from a middle order that was unable to fully cash in despite the strong foundation. KL Rahul chipped in with a valuable half-century, but with him batting at No.6, India might be looking for a quicker strike rate in the latter stages. The presence of Ravindra Jadeja continues to provide valuable balance, contributing both with the bat and as a key spinner. With New Raipur expected to offer a good batting surface, the hosts may also weigh the option of adding extra firepower by bringing in Rishabh Pant, whose ability to accelerate in the middle overs and finish strongly could prove decisive. With the ball, Kuldeep Yadav and Harshit Rana were the standout performers in the opener, turning the game on its head at crucial moments. However, the pace unit as a whole will be keen to be sharper at the death after South Africa threatened to pull off a remarkable chase. The Proteas arrive in New Raipur with a mix of confidence and disappointment. They showed tremendous fighting spirit in the first ODI, staying in the contest nearly all the way thanks to a brave late surge led by Marco Jansen and Corbin Bosch, both of whom struck impressive half-centuries under intense pressure. Their effort underlined the depth in South Africa’s batting and their willingness to battle till the very end. At the top, they will be hoping for steadier starts from experienced names like Quinton de Kock and Aiden Markram, while Matthew Breetzke and Dewald Brevis showed they possess the aggression to change the momentum in a matter of overs. The bowling, however, will need improvement, particularly against India’s top order. Prenelan Subrayen endured a tough outing in the series opener, and there could be a case for bringing in Keshav Maharaj to add control and experience through left-arm spin. The fast bowlers, too, will be eager to tighten up after being expensive through the middle and death overs. With India aiming to move closer to sealing the series and South Africa desperate to draw level, all signs point to another gripping contest. Fine margins, smart selections and composure in crunch moments will once again shape the outcome, and if the opening game was anything to go by, New Raipur is set for an evening of high-quality, high-pressure cricket.
